name: Italian lessons
about: The path through the first Italian words, a few at a time, each in everyday sentences written for its lesson. Word list: FrequencyWords by Hermit Dave, from OpenSubtitles (opensubtitles.org), CC BY-SA 4.0.

words.conoscere: to know, to be acquainted with
words.dal: from the; at the; to the
words.chiamarsi: to be called, to have as a name
words.mancare: to be missing, to be missed
words.glielo: it to him or to her
words.prendersi: to take for oneself; prendersi cura di = take care of
words.riflettere: to reflect, to think something over

ciao.about: To anyone you say tu to; it's also bye.

come-stai.about: Literally how stay you: to someone you say tu to.

dov-e.about: dove and è run together: where is.

ci-sono.about: Use ci sono with more than one person or thing.

lessons.title: Find the phone on the table

words.means: sul = on the (su and il run together)

concept.line: Every noun is an il word or a la word: il telefono, la borsa. Learn which with the word.
A question can keep a statement's order, with your voice rising: La macchina è qui? (the car is here?) A question word goes first: Dov'è la macchina?

words.means: mio = my (an il word: il mio); mia = my (a la word: la mia)
nella = in the (in and la run together)
you (to one person you know well)
pronto = ready (said of a man or an il word); pronta = ready (of a woman or a la word)

concept.line: The verb's ending already says who, so io and tu are left out unless it matters who: Sei pronto? (are ready?), Bevo caffè (drink coffee).
mio and mia come with the: il mio telefono, la mia chiave (the my phone: my phone).

words.means: the mother; mia madre = my mother

lessons.title: On the table, in the bag

concept.line: su, in and di run into the after them: sul tavolo (on the table), nella borsa (in the bag), la chiave della macchina (the key of the car). They're never written apart.

words.means: viene = comes (with lui, lei); vengo = come (with io); vieni = come (with tu)
too, also (before the word it's about: anche lei = her too)

concept.line: non goes right before the verb: Non bevo caffè (not I drink coffee). English says don't; Italian has only non.

words.means: voglio = want (with io); vuoi = want (with tu); vuole = wants (with lui, lei); vogliamo = want (with noi)

concept.line: After volere (want), the next verb stays in its basic form, ending in -re: Voglio mangiare (I want eat), Vogliamo bere un caffè.
The verb's ending says who: bevo (I drink), bevi (you drink), beve (he or she drinks); vengo, vieni, viene. That's why io and tu can be left out.

words.means: posso = can (with io); puoi = can (with tu); possiamo = can (with noi)
vado = go (with io); andiamo = go (with noi); va = goes (with lui, lei, Lei)
Lei = you (polite: to someone you don't know well)
so = know (with io); sa = knows (with lui, lei, Lei)

concept.line: Lei, often written with a capital L, is the polite you, to someone you don't know well. Its verb is the one for lui and lei: Lei sa dov'è? (she knows where is?)
questo goes with an il word and questa with a la word, for this: questo libro, questa chiave. On its own, questo is this one: Questo è un libro.

po' = a little (in un po' di)

the photo (also foto in the plural)

mi = to me (with piace or piacciono)
ti = to you (with piace or piacciono, to tu)

concept.line: The thing or activity you like is the subject: Mi piace stare a casa (I like staying home). mi means to me, ti to you, ci to us. One thing or an activity takes piace; more than one thing takes piacciono.

words.means: do = I give; dare = give (the infinitive)
parlare = talk; parliamo = we talk, let's talk
le = to her; Le = to you (polite)

concept.line: Many verbs say a completed event with avere and a past participle: Ho lavorato (I worked or have worked). A few, such as andare and venire, use essere instead. The helper changes with the person: hai lavorato, abbiamo lavorato. Learn irregular participles such as fatto with the verb.

lessons.title: What did you have for lunch?

concept.line: Many common verbs have irregular past participles: bevuto, letto, visto. Others follow a regular pattern: mangiato, comprato. With avere they describe completed events: Ho letto il libro; Abbiamo bevuto un caffè.

arrivato = arrived (masculine singular); arrivata = arrived (feminine singular), after essere
rimasto = stayed (masculine singular); rimasta = stayed (feminine singular), after essere
dal = to the, at the (da and il together, with a person); also from the

concept.line: andare, venire, arrivare and rimanere use essere in the past. The participle agrees with the subject: sono andato (a man), sono andata (a woman). Learn the helper with each verb: camminare uses avere, although it describes movement.

words.means: ascoltare = listen to; ascolto = I listen to; ascolti = you listen to

concept.line: Learn the link with each verb. aspettare and ascoltare take an object directly: Ti aspetto; Ascolto la musica. pensare takes a: Penso a te. parlare can take con for the person and di for the topic: Parliamo con lui; Parliamo del film.

words.means: solo = only, just (unchanging in this use)
può = can (with lui, lei, Lei or qualcuno)
alto = tall or high (masculine); alta = tall or high (feminine)
bella = beautiful (feminine); bello = beautiful (masculine, after the noun)

concept.line: Adjectives often follow the noun and agree with it: una casa piccola. Some commonly go before it too: una bella casa. Position alone does not make an adjective wrong.

words.means: nostro = our (masculine singular); nostra = our (feminine singular)

si chiama = is called, has the name

conosce = knows; with Lei, you know (polite)

al = to the, at the (a and il together)
male = pain in fare male: to hurt
fa = does, makes (third person singular); fa male = hurts

metta = put (Lei); mettete = put (voi); mettilo = put it (tu); mettetelo = put it (voi)

concept.line: Use the command for the listener: prendi (tu), prenda (polite Lei), prendete (voi). Short object pronouns attach to affirmative tu and voi commands: prendilo, mettetelo. With Lei they come before: lo metta. A negative tu command uses non plus the infinitive: non lanciare.

prenderti = pick you up; prendermi = pick me up (attached object pronouns)
significa = means (a word or a statement)

usare = use; uso = I use; usi = you use
provarlo = try it, with lo attached to the infinitive

dei = some (masculine plural); also of the
delle = some (feminine plural); also of the
sulla = about the, on the (su and la together)

concept.line: Many nouns change ending in the plural: libro becomes libri. foto stays foto: le foto. Articles and adjectives agree too: delle belle foto. qualche instead takes a singular noun even when it means a few: qualche libro.

words.means: ne = of them, of it (with a quantity)

concept.line: With a quantity, ne replaces a known noun: Ho due libri; ne ho due (I have two books; I have two). Put ne before the conjugated verb here. Keep the number or amount, including uno or una; English can leave of them unsaid.

words.means: tornare = return; torno = I return; torniamo = we return; tornato/tornata = returned (with essere)

concept.line: Learn the whole construction. In è sicuro camminare qui (it is safe to walk here), the infinitive names the activity and takes no preposition. In un libro difficile da capire (a book that is difficult to understand), da links the thing to what someone does to it. per gives a purpose; provare takes a.

the way, the manner; in modo diverso = differently

concept.line: Say io, tu, noi or voi when contrasting people or making clear who you mean: Voi andate, noi no. Otherwise the verb ending often gives enough information, so the subject can stay unsaid.

concept.line: For how someone feels, use sentirsi: mi sento, ti senti, si sente. The short pronoun points back to that person. Compare Sento il braccio, I can feel my arm, with Mi sento forte, I feel strong.

words.means: if; whether in an embedded question

tirare = pull; tira = pull (tu); tiro = I pull

dovuto = had to (past participle of dovere)
lasciami = let me (tu); lascio = I leave; lascia = leave (tu)
according to; secondo me = in my opinion

parla = he or she talks; parlano = they talk
sarò = I will be; sarà = will be (with lui, lei or a thing)

words.means: dimentico = I forget; dimenticato = forgotten; dimenticare = forget

era = was (with lui, lei or a thing); eravamo = we were
back then (referring to a past time)

mi sveglio = I wake up; ti svegli = you wake up

that, who, which (linking a noun to a description)
where (linking a place to a description)
morire = die; muore = dies; muoiono = they die
deve = must, has to (with lui, lei or Lei)
riesco = I manage; riusciamo = we manage; followed by a + infinitive
